title: ESPRA: ESP32 Speech and Proximity Roaming Assistant
summary: A voice-controlled ESP32-S3 robot that drives, turns toward whoever is speaking, and talks back in under 5 s.
details:
Built on my own, with help from an AI coding assistant on the firmware; the wiring, capacitors, testing and design calls were mine.

It's a differential-drive robot on an ESP32-S3: TB6612FNG motor control runs as a 50 Hz FreeRTOS task with soft-start ramping and a time-of-flight collision interlock, and two INMP441 mics use TDOA sound localization so it turns toward the speaker. The voice pipeline uses energy-based voice activity detection with adaptive noise tracking, Whisper speech-to-text with confidence filtering, an LLM for dialogue, and TTS streamed back to an I2S amplifier over a custom TCP protocol, replying in under 5 s.

I debugged the Wi-Fi audio link end to end, replacing a lock-step protocol with a length-framed, 4-chunk sliding window and underrun-safe buffering, which fixed hangs, desyncs and choppy playback.

I isolated intermittent resets to a shared power-bank rail by A/B testing on PC USB, then fixed them with bulk and decoupling capacitors, I2C pull-ups and motor soft-start, and added a task watchdog, I2C bus timeouts and Wi-Fi auto-recovery.

Earlier on, I traced an audio buzz to the speaker wiring and rewired the two 4 Ω speakers from parallel (2 Ω, below the MAX98357A's rated load) to series (8 Ω), and split audio and graphics across the two cores so OLED writes no longer interrupted the I2S stream.

title: Beehive Winter Monitoring System
summary: Led the electrical design of a ~$200 winter hive monitor, now being installed for UofT BEES.
details:
I led the electrical design on a team of 6, and helped with the firmware for the final build. The monitor places SCD41 CO2 and BME680 sensors in a vented in-hive enclosure and three DS18B20 probes on a shared 1-Wire bus, cabled through IP68 glands to an outdoor ESP32 enclosure that uploads data over Wi-Fi every hour.

I derived a 1.94 V/m E-field exposure limit from a published bee EMF stress study, then worked from dBm to watts, power density (S = PG/4πr²) and field strength (E = √(S·377 Ω)) to get an 11.2 cm minimum ESP32 distance at 2 dBm, confirmed by EMF meter readings of about 1 V/m.

I drew the schematics, sourced the BOM from DigiKey, and specified a 2 m shielded 6 × 22 AWG cable rated to -40 °C, with the shield grounded at the outdoor end only to avoid a ground loop. I ran the I2C bus at 50 kHz across the cable, checking rise time stayed under 1 µs with about 450 pF of bus capacitance, and budgeted about 2.1 Ah over 150 days against about 3 Ah from lithium cells rated to -40 °C.

I also wrote a step-by-step build guide and a net-by-net wiring reference so club members with no soldering experience could build and install it.

title: Embedded Systems Intern
summary: Cut load-cell noise from ±1 g to ±50 mg, drew a full transmitter schematic, and assembled 100+ boards.
details:
I wired the load cell and wrote the firmware for a stepper-driven dispenser that dispenses by weight, testing NAU7802 and HX711 24-bit ADCs. Measuring noise from thousands of samples, I reduced it from ±1 g to ±50 mg by proposing an LDO supply, which halved the noise on its own, then moving the decoupling caps to the ADC pins and enabling the PGA filter cap on the unused channel.

I drew the Altium schematic for an internal RC aircraft transmitter (ESP32, RYLR993 LoRa module, USB-to-SPI joystick bridge), building every symbol and footprint from scratch with JLCPCB part numbers for direct BOM ordering.

I also assembled 100+ boards for a medical project using stencil paste reflow and hand soldering, then tested each one and fixed shorted rails, cold joints and reversed diodes.

title: Size-Targeted JPEG Compression
summary: Modified JPEG so you set the output file size instead of a quality level; predicted size within 5.6% on average.
details:
I modified JPEG so the user sets the output file size instead of a quality level, using Lagrange multipliers to choose the quantization table scale and zero-rounding threshold that minimize mean squared error at that size.

I developed a size estimation method by modeling DCT coefficients with a Laplacian distribution (b = √2/σ) and deriving a 3.295-bit average Huffman code length from the ITU-T T.81 tables, giving a closed-form model, size ≈ 3.295 · n · exp(−Tb). Tested on 5 of my own photos, it predicted compressed size within 5.6% on average, with errors from 0.49% to 10.35%.

I cut the MATLAB solver's runtime from failing to finish overnight to 2.6 s by factoring the symbolic variables out of million-term sums, and wrote it all up in a ~4,000-word research report with guidance from a mathematics mentor.

title: School AI Backend
summary: A study assistant backend built with an AI coding assistant; I use it dozens of times a day.
details:
Built on my own with an AI coding assistant: a FastAPI service that syncs student-visible Canvas course content, indexes it for retrieval, and serves it to a Custom GPT, with every result carrying its source URL.

Each sync treats Canvas as a graph, recording links between resources, versioning changed content and chunking it for search. Search combines an English full-text (tsvector) index with exact pgvector cosine similarity in PostgreSQL. Syncs are idempotent, using canonical resource keys and content hashes, and only transient errors are retried.

It also handles Google Calendar operations with validation and audit rows.

It runs as a stateless, non-root Docker container on Google Cloud Run with secrets in Secret Manager, with Cloud Scheduler running incremental syncs every 4 hours and a full sync daily. I wrote pytest unit tests for pagination, link discovery, calendar validation, chunking and auth.

title: CNC Programmer
summary: Programmed and ran CNC cuts for 3 whole-house and 5+ smaller cabinetry projects, over $100K CAD.
details:
I programmed and ran CNC cuts in Mozaik CAD/CAM from architectural drawings for 3 whole-house and 5+ smaller residential projects (over $100K CAD), often working alone in the shop.

I built parametric cabinet templates driven by algebraic constraints that adjust in all three dimensions, and they're still in use.

I caught incorrect measurements and tool geometries in G-code, along with cutting blade issues, before they reached production. I also optimized part nesting to minimize offcut waste and planned under-cabinet LED lighting against residential electrical drawings.

title: Clip-On Tablet Stand
summary: A 3D-printed stand that clips onto a keyboard so a tablet can replace a laptop.
details:
I modeled a tablet stand in Autodesk Fusion around a photo of the keyboard, and 3D printed it on my own printer. To save time and filament, I fit tested with narrow printed strips before printing the full part.

I also designed a locking mechanism with friction-fit blocks that attaches to a separate adjustable stand. I built and used it as a laptop replacement.

title: Creation of Custom Keyboard and Data Cable
summary: Soldered and assembled a functional keyboard and accompanying cable.
details:
Responsible for planning, purchasing and assembling parts.

Build process involved manual lubrication and soldering of switches, as well as cutting, wrapping, and soldering the cable.
